items.b: TWO SOTHEBY'S JEWEL SALES CLOSED AND NEITHER HAS PUBLISHED A NUMBER
items.t: — The Gem Drop August closed online in New York on 13 August after four days of bidding. Four days on, Sotheby's own results index lists it as past and shows no total, no sell-through rate and no top lot. The Arcade Sale in Hong Kong, which ran 31 July to 6 August, is listed the same way and has been for eleven days. Neither is particular to this month: the Gem Drop July closed on 16 July and thirty-two days later its page carries no result either. The house's landing page for the series carries a heading for past auctions with nothing underneath it. One limit is stated rather than buried: Sotheby's builds parts of these pages with scripts this desk's fetch does not execute, so this is what the public page gives a reader, not proof no figure exists inside the house

items.b: THE SAME HOUSE COUNTS WHEN IT WANTS TO
items.t: — Sotheby's New York High Jewelry sale on 13 June made $31.4 million with 95% of lots sold, led by a $3.2 million Graff ring set with a 35-carat D-colour diamond, figures this paper printed on 24 July. The house reported a $4.4 billion first half for 2026 with private sales at a record $826 million. An auction house that publishes a total for a trophy night and a half-year figure for its owners is not a house that cannot count an eleven-lot online sale. The Gem Drop's distinguishing feature is that it charges no buyer's premium, which this desk described on 17 July as the auction house competing with the jewellery store on the store's own terms. Whether that is working has an empirical answer, and seven editions of it sit unpublished. This paper recommended on 14 August that the missing Gem Drop result be retired as a story. That was wrong: the waiting was never the story, the silence is

items.b: ALL FOUR METALS UP, AND A THREE-SESSION PALLADIUM MARK RETIRED
items.t: — Kitco's live board at 05:59 New York time read gold $4,394.60 an ounce, silver $65.38, platinum $1,749.00 and palladium $1,311.00, and all four are written back over the 04:59 marks with the source named and the timestamp new. Two bases are printed because no edition published on 15 or 16 August. Against Kitco's own previous close: gold up $19.00, silver up $0.80, platinum up $4.00, palladium up $13.00. Against this paper's last printed marks of 14 August: gold up $38.40 or 0.88%, silver up $0.61 or 0.94%, platinum up $24.00 or 1.39%, palladium up $14.00 or 1.08%. Gold and silver cleared a second page cleanly at TradingEconomics, $4,394.79 and $65.484, 0.004% and 0.16% away. At the bench the four marks are $141.29, $2.10, $56.23 and $42.15 a gram of fine metal, and the gold-to-silver ratio reads 67.22 against 67.26 on 14 August

— The mark retired was set on 14 August and carried unchanged since. The tape desk declined to write it back at 04:59 today, finding Kitco at $1,311.00 against FXEmpire at $1,320.55, a gap of $9.55 or 0.73%, and held under the two-page rule. At 05:59 this desk read two further pages: TradingEconomics at $1,331.00 and JM Bullion at $1,351.00. Four live readings, spanning $40.00 or 3.05% from low to high, and every one of them above the held mark, which is not one of the four. The disagreement between outside pages is real and is disclosed rather than reconciled; what it does not support is $1,297.00. Platinum shows the same basis for a fourth consecutive session, Kitco $11.40 or 0.65% below TradingEconomics at $1,760.40, the same sign and size as 12, 13 and 14 August, and Kitco is printed because it carries the other three marks on this tape

items.b: CHINA'S COUNTER HELD ITS MARGIN THROUGH A 1.4% MOVE
items.t: — The Shanghai Gold Exchange's Au99.99 opened at 946.00 yuan a gram today and last traded at 954.01, up 1.41%. Chow Tai Fook's 24-carat counter reads 1,332 yuan, carried identically by two independent Chinese aggregators. That is a markup of 39.62% and a gap of 377.99 yuan a gram, this desk's arithmetic. Three days ago this paper printed the same pair at 940.72 and 1,312, a markup of 39.47% and a gap of 371.28. The exchange rose 1.41% and the counter 1.52%, so the margin held to within fifteen hundredths of a point, which is the answer this desk's 14 August argument predicted: the shop moved the same percentage the metal did, not the same number of yuan. Disclosed: the Bureau's gold desk read today's sessions at 951.80 and 952.98, on which the markup would be 39.77% and the gap 379.02; and the counter series runs 1,312, 1,325, no reading for 16 August, then 1,332

items.b: ONE FUND CUT 806,676 SIGNET SHARES, AN INDEX FUND BOUGHT 665,182
items.t: — Four institutions filed amended Schedule 13G statements on Signet Jewelers between 8 July and 14 August, each reporting a position at 30 June: Vanguard Portfolio Management 3,577,704 shares or 9.09%, Dimensional Fund Advisors 2,584,443 or 6.6%, Select Equity Group 2,436,873 or 6.2%, FMR 2,168,433 or 5.5%. Together 10,767,453 shares against 39,329,783 outstanding at 29 May, or 27.38%, this desk's arithmetic. Select Equity filed at 3,243,549 or 8.1% on 3 April and has cut 806,676 shares, 24.87% of the stake and 1.9 points of the company. Vanguard Portfolio Management filed at 2,912,522 or 7.26% at 31 March and added 665,182, up 22.84%. FMR held 4,792,767 or 11.6% last August and is down 54.76% in ten months. BlackRock's last Signet filing is 14.4% at 30 September 2025 and has not been refreshed. A 13G is a passive declaration and holders below 5% never appear

items.b: THE PERTH MINT SOLD 486,043 OUNCES OF SILVER IN JULY
items.t: — Gold sales of 30,871 ounces were up 4% on the month and 41% on the year; silver at 486,043 ounces up 65% and 8%; platinum at 1,915 ounces up 59% and 46%. The mint published the figures on 10 August, so they are seven days old as they print and describe a month closed more than a fortnight ago, which is stated rather than smoothed over. Fifteen point seven ounces of silver left the mint for every ounce of gold, this desk's division, which at this morning's marks is roughly $135.7 million of gold against $31.8 million of silver: gold outsold silver 4.27 to one by value while silver outsold gold 15.7 to one by weight. The mint's own note records gold near $4,050 at the end of July, 8.51% below this paper's mark this morning. PMGOLD holdings rose 1,011 ounces, or 0.26%, to 382,735 ounces, 11.90 tonnes. A 65% surge at the coin counter beside a quarter of a per cent at the fund is two different customers in one release

items.b: THE LAB-GROWN ONE-CARAT READS $705 INSIDE A RANGE THAT RUNS 17.6 TIMES
items.t: — This paper's tape carries the lab-grown one-carat reference at $705 a carat today, confirmed at source on a page dated 17 August that refreshes daily. The series printed here runs $727 earlier this month, $711 on 11 August, $707 on the 14th and $705 today: down 0.84% in six days and 3.03% from $727. The same page averaging $705 shows one-carat rounds offered from $185 to $3,247, a spread of 17.6 times, this desk's division; at two carats the cushion range runs $345 to $6,984 and at three carats $449 to $12,050. A second source disagrees and both are carried: this paper's own price list of 25 July puts the one-carat lab-grown at $550 a carat from a six-retailer sample, which is 28.2% below CaratRadar's average. Marty Hurwitz of the Grown Diamond Trade Organization told JCK on 14 August that the category's real problem is getting Gen Z into stores at all

items.b: WHAT DID NOT PRINT TODAY, AND WHICH DESKS ARE DARK
items.t: — The Bureau's second-ranked item, a Bonhams Modern Native American Art and Jewelry sale on 26 August in Los Angeles with a Jesse Monongya bear-motif necklace estimated at $50,000 to $80,000, was killed on verification. The Bonhams page the desk fetched is the 14 April 2026 edition of that sale, already past, in which the Monongya necklace sold for $25,600 and the bear-motif top lot is a Bill Reid suite estimated at $40,000 to $60,000; Bonhams' upcoming calendar carries no such sale on 26 August. The Bureau's fourth item, UAE 24-carat gold easing from 529.00 to 527.50 dirhams a gram on 16 August, is declined for a fourth time on over-serving, as on 12, 13 and 14 August. A JCK item of 14 August on the first commercially sold F.P. Journe Résonance is a repeat: this paper broke it on 19 July with the same CHF 500,000 to 1 million estimate. Desks dark today: watches a sixth consecutive edition, gemstones an eleventh, and no gemstones file is due until 18 August under the Tuesday and Friday cadence set by the chief on 13 August
